label: Stop 3: The Zuiderkerk, the South Church

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Oh, that's pretty. It looks like a wedding cake.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Good eye. That's Renaissance style, in brick and stone.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The architect was Hendrick de Keyser.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was built from 1603 to 1611.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The tower came later, finished in 1614.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And it's called the South Church because it's in the south.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Of the city, as it was then. Yes.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was the first new Protestant church built in Amsterdam.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Wait, is that in the record?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a common claim in guides.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Our fact sources for this walk don't state it, so take it as a guide's claim.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The dates and the architect, we can state.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Good. I like a Ben who admits it.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Now, De Keyser himself. He died in 1621, and he's buried in this church.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: The architect, buried in his own building.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. That's the record.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: It's a nice thing to have.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Now we come to the sad part. This part has no jokes.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Three of Rembrandt's children are buried here.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Rembrandt lived very close, on the Jodenbreestraat, just a short distance from this church.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Three children.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. We know that from the church's own history.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We won't guess anything more about them.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And there's more.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In the winter of 1944 to 1945, the Hunger Winter, the church was used as a temporary morgue.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: People were dying faster than they could be buried.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's very recent.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It is. Some of the people alive in this city today remember it, or their parents do.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's a different kind of haunted.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. Not a ghost story. A memory.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: How long did it work as a church?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Services ended in 1929. The building closed in 1970.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: After renovation from 1976 to 1979, it opened as a municipal information center in 1988.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It still has that role, with exhibitions.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the tower has bells.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A carillon, installed in 1656 by the Hemony brothers, famous bell makers.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: If you're lucky, you might hear it.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's not guaranteed.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Is there a legend?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Again, we looked. Nothing well-sourced that we can pass on.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We'd rather say that than make something up.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Pause for a moment, everyone.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Look up at the tower against the night sky.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Good moment for it.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And then?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Then we head back toward the old center, west.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You're going to the Oude Kerk.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Old Church. Walk back past the Waag, then west through the lanes.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Keep the map open, because the streets bend.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The church tower stands in a small square, with buildings tight all around it.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And what's the area like?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Lively. It's the red light district.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We'll talk about that when we're there.
